title: Patch: a co-op game won on one board says which board and how

**Issue #3697 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3697: Patch: a co-op game won on one board says which board and how
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
In co-op, two players fight an AI team on two boards side by side. When the game ends because of something on one board (a card's own win condition, a player voted out, a hero escaping the universe), the result panel says only "One of the duels decided the game." Neither player learns which board it was or what happened, though the one-on-one result screen already has words for every one of those endings. Once this is built, the panel says, for example, "On your teammate's board: their opponent was voted out of the game."

## Why
- `apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.tsx:155-156` maps every `duelResult` to `t("One of the duels decided the game.")`.
- The engine gives `duelResult` to every duel ending but the turn cap, the time ceiling and a Glitch (`crates/engine/src/duos/reduce.rs:446-455`): a held alternative win and a win by effect (R850), voted out and both voted out (R1843000, R1843001), fled and fled-decisive (R1843002), the endings the Stinkyscape set's cards bring. SPEC §13.4's table lists it as "A seat holding a win at its duel's game-end point".
- The co-op view already holds both duels' views, `own` and `teammate`, each a `PlayerView` with its own `result` (`apps/web/src/wire/generated/DuosView.ts`), and `resultReason` (`apps/web/src/game/Result.tsx:44-88`) already words each of these reasons for one seat.
- The co-op turn-cap line, "The game reached its turn limit." (`DuosBoard.tsx:153-154`), differs from the 1v1 and practice line "The turn limit was reached." (`Result.tsx:55-56`, `apps/web/src/practice/PracticeResult.tsx:45-46`).

## Proposal
For `duelResult`, find the duel whose `result` is set, your own first, and name the board and the reason: "On your board: …" in `resultReason`'s words from your seat, "On your teammate's board: …" in words written for the teammate's side (new strings, since "you" there is the teammate). Keep today's line as the fallback when neither duel's result is set, and use the 1v1 turn-cap words. Every new string gets its zh-CN entry (R711000). This is presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.tsx`, `apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.test.tsx`, `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`
- SPEC §13.4; R850, R1843000, R1843001, R1843002, R711000

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With `result.reason` `duelResult` and your own duel's result an alt-win, the reason names your board and your winning condition.
- [ ] With the teammate's duel's result voted-out, it names the teammate's board and who was voted out, from the teammate's side.
- [ ] With neither duel's result set, the old line shows.
- [ ] The co-op turn-cap line reads as the 1v1 one does.
- [ ] Every new `t()` key has its zh-CN entry, and `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/duos/DuosBoard.test.tsx src/i18n/i18n.test.ts` passes.

## Size and risks
Small: one function, a handful of strings and their tests. The teammate's-board wording must not reuse the one-seat sentences as they stand, or "You were voted out" would describe the teammate.

## Goal

When a co-op game ends with the team reason `duelResult`, the result panel's reason line names the board that decided it and how. It uses the seat's own duel first, then the teammate's duel, in these words:
- Own board: "On your board: you met your winning condition." The words come from the 1v1 `resultReason` as it stands.
- Teammate's board: "On your teammate's board: their opponent was voted out of the game." These words are new and written for the teammate's side.
- Neither duel's `result` set, or a teammate ending with no words below: the old line "One of the duels decided the game." stays.

The co-op `turnCap` line becomes the 1v1 line "The turn limit was reached." Every new `t()` key gets a zh-CN entry (R711000). This is presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

1. **`apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`.** In the co-op result block (around line 1275):

   - After it, add these 12 entries exactly (keep the file's 2-space indent and commas):
   ```
   "On your board: {reason}": "你的棋盘上：{reason}",
   "On your teammate's board: {reason}": "队友的棋盘上：{reason}",
   "Your teammate met their winning condition.": "你的队友达成了胜利条件。",
   "Their opponent met their own winning condition.": "队友的对手达成了自己的胜利条件。",
   "Your teammate's card won the game.": "你队友的卡牌赢得了对局。",
   "Their opponent's card won the game.": "队友对手的卡牌赢得了对局。",
   "Their opponent was voted out of the game.": "队友的对手被投票移出了对局。",
   "Your teammate was voted out of the game.": "你的队友被投票移出了对局。",
   "Your teammate escaped the universe. Their opponent draws.": "你的队友逃离了宇宙。队友的对手算作平局。",
   "Their opponent escaped the universe. Your teammate draws.": "队友的对手逃离了宇宙。你的队友算作平局。",
   "Your teammate escaped the universe and left their opponent behind.": "你的队友逃离了宇宙，把对手留在了身后。",
   "Their opponent escaped the universe and left your teammate behind.": "队友的对手逃离了宇宙，把你的队友留在了身后。"
   ```

   - The neutral sentences reused below ("Both players met a winning condition.", "Both players were voted out together.", "Both players escaped the universe.") already have entries.

2. **`DuosBoard.tsx` imports.**
   - Add `import { outcomeFor, resultReason, type ResultOutcome } from "../game/Result.tsx";`, next to the `Game` import.
   - Delete `import type { Team } from "../wire/generated/Team.ts";`. Its only use was `resultWords`' signature, and the unused import would fail eslint.

3. **`DuosBoard.tsx`, new helpers directly above `resultWords`.** Copy this exactly:
   ```ts
   type DuelResult = NonNullable<PlayerView["result"]>;

   /** The first letter in lower case, so a sentence reads after "On your board:"; a script with no case is unchanged. */
   function lowerFirst(text: string): string {
     return text.charAt(0).toLowerCase() + text.slice(1);
   }

   /**
    * #3697: how the teammate's duel ended, in the teammate's seat's words ("you" there is the teammate); `outcome` is the
    * teammate's own (`outcomeFor`, R1843004). Only the endings a duel hands the game by `duelResult` and the issue lists
    * have words (R850, R1843000, R1843001, R1843002); null for the rest, so the caller keeps its old line.
    */
   function teammateReason(outcome: ResultOutcome, result: DuelResult): string | null {
     switch (result.reason) {
       case "alt-win":
         if (outcome === "draw") return t("Both players met a winning condition.");
         return outcome === "win"
           ? t("Your teammate met their winning condition.")
           : t("Their opponent met their own winning condition.");
       case "won-by-effect":
         return outcome === "win" ? t("Your teammate's card won the game.") : t("Their opponent's card won the game.");
       case "voted-out":
         return outcome === "win" ? t("Their opponent was voted out of the game.") : t("Your teammate was voted out of the game.");
       case "both-voted-out":
         return t("Both players were voted out together.");
       case "fled":
         if (outcome === "win") return t("Your teammate escaped the universe. Their opponent draws.");
         return result.winner === "draw"
           ? t("Both players escaped the universe.")
           : t("Their opponent escaped the universe. Your teammate draws.");
       case "fled-decisive":
         return outcome === "win"
           ? t("Your teammate escaped the universe and left their opponent behind.")
           : t("Their opponent escaped the universe and left your teammate behind.");
       default:
         return null;
     }
   }

   /** #3697: why a `duelResult` ended the game: the board whose duel ended, the seat's own first, and how. */
   function duelReason(view: DuosView): string {
     const own = view.own.result;
     if (own !== null) {
       const why = t(resultReason(outcomeFor(own, view.own.viewer), own.reason, own.winner));
       return t("On your board: {reason}", { reason: lowerFirst(why) });
     }
     const mate = view.teammate.result;
     const said = mate === null ? null : teammateReason(outcomeFor(mate, view.teammate.viewer), mate);
     return said === null ? t("One of the duels decided the game.") : t("On your teammate's board: {reason}", { reason: lowerFirst(said) });
   }
   ```
   - Every sentence stays a literal inside `t()`, so `i18n.test.ts`'s static scan holds each to a zh-CN entry. `t(resultReason(...))` is dynamic, as in `Result.tsx`, and its keys exist.
   - `view.own.viewer` and `view.teammate.viewer` are both the team's `PlayerId`, so each call gives that seat's own outcome.

4. **`DuosBoard.tsx`, `resultWords`.**
   - Change the signature to `function resultWords(result: DuosResult, view: DuosView): {…same return type…}` and add `const team = teamOf(view.seat);` as its first line, replacing the old `team` parameter.
   - `case "turnCap"`: `t("The turn limit was reached.")`.
   - `case "duelResult"`: `reason: duelReason(view)`.
   - Update both callers. In `ResultPanel`, `resultWords(view.result, view)`. In the rail, `resultWords(view.result, view).heading`.

5. **`apps/web/README.md`.** After the Duos list's "on a live game's result, Play again …" bullet (ends "no button."), add:
   ```
   - a game a duel's ending decided (`duelResult`) says which board and how in its result panel (#3697): "On your board: …"

     teammate's side (`DuosBoard.tsx`'s `teammateReason`), else the old "One of the duels decided the game."; the turn cap
     reads as the 1v1 one does.
   ```

6. **`spec/13-duos.md` §13.4.** Add this paragraph just before "A disconnect never ends a co-op game ([[§13.8]])." Then re-read that line's links:
   ```

   ```

## Tests

File: `apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.test.tsx`. Append one `describe("#3697 the result panel names the board whose duel decided a duelResult game", …)`. Use `#3697` titles, not `R<n>` ones: a new `R` title would need a ruling note. Reuse `duosView()` and `renderDuosBoard()`.

Helpers inside the describe:
```ts
type Ended = NonNullable<PlayerView["result"]>;
function decided(own: Ended | null, teammate: Ended | null, reason = "duelResult", winner: "a" | "b" = "a"): DuosView {
  const base = duosView();
  return { ...base, own: { ...base.own, result: own }, teammate: { ...base.teammate, result: teammate },
    result: { outcome: "win", winner, reason } };
}
async function reasonLine(view: DuosView): Promise<string | null> {
  renderDuosBoard({ view });
  await act(async () => {});   // the board's MutationObserver reports before the panel mounts
  return screen.getByTestId("duos-result").querySelector(".duos-result__reason")?.textContent ?? null;
}
```
Assert on `.duos-result__reason` only. The board's own 1v1 result chip also prints sentences, so asserting on the whole page would be ambiguous. Use exact `toBe`.

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `#3697 your own board's alt-win names your board and your winning condition` | `decided({winner:"p1",reason:"alt-win"}, null)` gives "On your board: you met your winning condition." |
| `#3697 your own board comes first when both duels have ended` | own `{p1, voted-out}`, teammate `{p2, alt-win}` gives "On your board: your opponent was voted out of the game." |
| `#3697 your own board's flight reads as the seat's draw` | own `{winner:"p2", reason:"fled"}` gives "On your board: your opponent escaped the universe. You draw." |
| `#3697 the teammate's voted-out names their board and who was voted out, from their side` | Teammate `{p1, voted-out}` gives "On your teammate's board: their opponent was voted out of the game." After `cleanup()`, teammate `{p2, voted-out}` with `winner:"b"` gives "On your teammate's board: your teammate was voted out of the game." and the line does not contain "You were". |
| `#3697 every teammate-side ending has its own words` | `it.each` table, teammate result `{winner, reason}` to expected line. Each expected line starts "On your teammate's board: ". |
| `#3697 with neither duel's result set the old line shows` | `decided(null, null)` gives "One of the duels decided the game." After `cleanup()`, a teammate result with no words (`{winner:"draw", reason:"turn-cap"}`) gives the same line. |
| `#3697 the co-op turn cap reads as the 1v1 line` | `{...duosView(), result:{outcome:"draw", winner:null, reason:"turnCap"}}` gives "The turn limit was reached." |
| `#3697 the line reads in Chinese, the board's label first` | See below. |

Table rows for the `it.each` test (teammate viewer is `p1`, so `winner:"p1"` is the teammate's win; the quoted text follows the common prefix):
- `alt-win`/`p1`: "your teammate met their winning condition."
- `alt-win`/`p2`: "their opponent met their own winning condition."
- `alt-win`/`draw`: "both players met a winning condition."
- `won-by-effect`/`p1`: "your teammate's card won the game."
- `won-by-effect`/`p2`: "their opponent's card won the game."
- `both-voted-out`/`draw`: "both players were voted out together."
- `fled`/`p1`: "your teammate escaped the universe. Their opponent draws."
- `fled`/`p2`: "their opponent escaped the universe. Your teammate draws."
- `fled`/`draw`: "both players escaped the universe."
- `fled-decisive`/`p1`: "your teammate escaped the universe and left their opponent behind."
- `fled-decisive`/`p2`: "their opponent escaped the universe and left your teammate behind."

The Chinese test:
- Start with `vi.useRealTimers()`, because `beforeEach` installed fake timers and `setLocale` loads its dictionary with a dynamic import.
- Then `await setLocale("zh-CN")` and `onTestFinished(resetLocaleForTests)`, both imported from `../i18n/i18n.ts`.
- Teammate `{p1, voted-out}` should read "队友的棋盘上：队友的对手被投票移出了对局。".
- Own `{p1, alt-win}` should read "你的棋盘上：你达成了胜利条件。".
- If setting the locale under this file's timers proves awkward, keep the English tests and drop only this one; `i18n.test.ts` still guards the keys.

Commands:
- `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` first. The web tests need the WASM package, and it is not built in this worktree.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/duos/DuosBoard.test.tsx src/i18n/i18n.test.ts`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/duos`
- `cargo jackioh spec check`, since a spec note was edited and R-ids are cited in code.

## Done when

- [ ] An own-duel alt-win names "your board" and your winning condition.
- [ ] A teammate-duel voted-out names "your teammate's board" and who was voted out, from the teammate's side, with no "You were voted out" for the teammate.
- [ ] With neither duel's result set, the old line shows.
- [ ] The co-op turn-cap line reads "The turn limit was reached."
- [ ] Every new `t()` key has a zh-CN entry and the dead key is gone; `DuosBoard.test.tsx` and `i18n.test.ts` pass.
- [ ] Typecheck, eslint, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass; the harness's web tests run.
- [ ] `git status` shows only the five files above. No `apps/web/src/wire/` change, no `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/` change.

## Risks

- **A pronoun slip.** The teammate table must never reuse the 1v1 "You …" sentences. The test table pins each one.
- **Hidden information.** The panel reads only `view.own.result` and `view.teammate.result`, which the view already carries; no hidden card is read.
- **Both duels ended at once, disagreeing.** The engine (`reduce.rs:446-474`) then draws, keeping the first duel's reason. The panel still names the seat's own duel first, as the issue asks. Not handled further.
- **Fled and the heading.** A co-op `duelResult` team result is the fleer's team's win. So "Your teammate draws." can sit under "Your team lost". That is R1843004's per-seat draw, kept on purpose.
- **The `lowerFirst` helper.** It lowers only the first letter of an already translated sentence. English "You …" becomes "you …", and Chinese is unchanged. A second sentence ("Your opponent draws.") keeps its capital.
- **Test timing.** If the panel is not mounted after `render`, the board is still busy. Add `await act(async () => { await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(10_000); })`, as the `#1146` test does.

## Open questions

None. Decisions the builder should keep in the PR description:
- The board label and the reason are composed from one prefix key plus the reason sentence, not one key per case. This avoids about 25 duplicate strings. The cost is the lower-casing helper.
- The teammate table covers only the six endings the issue lists. Hero death, concede, draw offers and disconnect cannot reach a duo duel's `duelResult` (concede and draw offers are refused, B10), and the turn cap, ceiling and Glitch are mapped to their own reasons. Those fall back to the old line.
- No new ruling and no patch fragment: this is presentation, and no catalog data changes.
````

   ```ts
   type DuelResult = NonNullable<PlayerView["result"]>;

   /** The first letter in lower case, so a sentence reads after "On your board:"; a script with no case is unchanged. */
   function lowerFirst(text: string): string {
     return text.charAt(0).toLowerCase() + text.slice(1);
   }

   /**

   function teammateReason(outcome: ResultOutcome, result: DuelResult): string | null {
     switch (result.reason) {
       case "alt-win":
         if (outcome === "draw") return t("Both players met a winning condition.");
         return outcome === "win"
           ? t("Your teammate met their winning condition.")
           : t("Their opponent met their own winning condition.");
       case "won-by-effect":
         return outcome === "win" ? t("Your teammate's card won the game.") : t("Their opponent's card won the game.");
       case "voted-out":
         return outcome === "win" ? t("Their opponent was voted out of the game.") : t("Your teammate was voted out of the game.");
       case "both-voted-out":
         return t("Both players were voted out together.");
       case "fled":
         if (outcome === "win") return t("Your teammate escaped the universe. Their opponent draws.");
         return result.winner === "draw"
           ? t("Both players escaped the universe.")
           : t("Their opponent escaped the universe. Your teammate draws.");
       case "fled-decisive":
         return outcome === "win"
           ? t("Your teammate escaped the universe and left their opponent behind.")
           : t("Their opponent escaped the universe and left your teammate behind.");
       default:
         return null;
     }
   }

   /** #3697: why a `duelResult` ended the game: the board whose duel ended, the seat's own first, and how. */
   function duelReason(view: DuosView): string {
     const own = view.own.result;
     if (own !== null) {
       const why = t(resultReason(outcomeFor(own, view.own.viewer), own.reason, own.winner));
       return t("On your board: {reason}", { reason: lowerFirst(why) });
     }
     const mate = view.teammate.result;
     const said = mate === null ? null : teammateReason(outcomeFor(mate, view.teammate.viewer), mate);
     return said === null ? t("One of the duels decided the game.") : t("On your teammate's board: {reason}", { reason: lowerFirst(said) });
   }
   ```
